key_insight: Detonation-spraying settings strongly control the balance between density, hardness, friction, and wear in self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings, creating a clear process-property trade-off.
engineering_relevance: The results provide practical parameter guidance for restoring and strengthening machine components with nickel-based coatings, where service performance depends on selecting the right spraying window.
method: Changed inter-shot delay from 0 to 1 s
evidence_signal: Microstructure, roughness, hardness, friction, and wear were evaluated; the best wear resistance reached a specific wear rate of 0.000189 mm³/(N·m), while the lowest friction was at 48% filling and O/C = 1.026.
watch_item: Lower friction conditions increased wear, so coating optimization must be application-specific rather than targeting a single metric.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
